question.problem: Expressed in terms of natural logarithms, what value of $x$ satisfies the equation ${e}^{x+2}=5\cdot {6}^{x}?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we take the natural logarithm $(ln)$ of both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{x+2} & =5\cdot {6}^{x} \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x+2}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5\cdot {6}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the fact that $\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{a})=a$ to simplify the left-hand side. This gives:

$$
x+2=\operatorname{ln}⁡(5\cdot {6}^{x})\,
$$

Next, we use the power and product laws of logarithms to simplify the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+\operatorname{ln}⁡({6}^{x}) \\ x+2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we solve for $x$, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+2 & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)+x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) \\ x-x\operatorname{ln}⁡(6) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-2 \\ x(1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-2 \\ x & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡(5)-2}{1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(6)}\end{aligned}
$$
